title: Does not sync between devices
body: 18 January 2025: I purchased a subscription to this app more than a year ago and despite its ease of use, IT STILL DOES NOT STAY IN SYNC BETWEEN DEVICES. I have written multiple times; however, the developer does not reply or respond to suggestions. Honestly, the fact that the app does not sync in this day and age is just really stupid. It is extremely aggravating. Additionally there isn’t any provision to import or export files so that you can manually keep devices in sync. When I try to convert measurements to another standard (Metric <—> Imperial), the app asks me to subscribe to enable the features including unit conversion. I ALREADY HAVE A SUBSCRIPTION !!! Set a program flag to avoid nagging a user to subscribe when they already are subscribed. The app always assumes the quantity of the recipe is in servings. Hello … wake up developer. Recipes for sauces, salsas, and other condiments are not measured in servings they are measured by volumes. If entering a recipe manually because the app cannot find a recipe on a webpage, you have to cut & paste ingredient by ingredient, direction by direction which is OK; however, each and every item you paste pops up the nagging question of whether you want to allow or not allow the paste which gets pretty old really fast. Snagging recipes off the internet is a hit or miss proposition. Way too many sites pasted in come back stating ‘recipe cannot be found’ even though in plain sight. Nice idea; but, half-baked at best and tjis was the primary reason for getting this app and subscribing. Suggested update features never seem to come into being with voting system and developers never reply back to issues, bugs, or suggestions. Now I lay the bread to rest; Just the Recipe passed not tests. So I part the usage and delete this app and turn to one that is better conceived, engineered, programmed, and UATed for proper UC and UE. ‘Just the Recipe’ seems smooth on the durface; but, it is fraught with issues and the lack of proper Use Cases in development. My advice: LOOK FOR SOMETHING ELSE.

title: Finally, a Way to Make Web Recipes Readable
body: I don’t even bother to try to read a web recipe anymore on its native page. The ads. The fluff. The overlays. The way they provide ingredients without the measurements until deep into the page. They’re insufferable. Instead of wading into the morass, I immediately feed the URL into Just the Recipe and it clears the clutter and provides the recipe in a clear, readable format. I can save it if it’s useful or dump it if not. It’s never once failed me. So why not 5 stars? My only complaint is the UI. Editing a recipe is clunky. Each line is in a text box with limited space. I find that a big drawback; I may want to say that it was too salty, that it needed cooking longer, that I added a good herb, or it worked well in my cast iron pan or air fryer, or similar observation. I can do all these things, but it’s a hassle. Its clunky. It is nevertheless the best Internet tool for cooking I’ve seen. No home cook who hunts the web for interesting recipes should be without it. Fix the editing feature and I’d happily give it five stars.

title: Perfect App Name for a Great Recipe App

But that just changed! Most all recipe manager apps attempt to do too many things, and they end up failing in their intended purpose of managing recipes. I've always wanted a simple, yet elegant recipe management solution with a beautiful UI and truly functional UX – and I just discovered it with this app! I don't want the unnecessary glitz of things like rating stars, etc. Every recipe I care enough about to save is obviously 5 stars. The iOS and iPadOS apps appear to be web-based apps, but in this case, that's a good thing, because the UI/UX familiarities are consistent between the apps and the website. I made a quick Safari web app of the web version, and it works flawlessly, leaving Safari free for other things. If you use Chrome, you can do the same thing.
